description: A promise floor names why and names the outs. `async` is erased in a `.d.ts`, so a bodyless promise-returning callee floors on *both* channels — it may sync-throw and it may reject — and each is bridged differently; the manifest's `async` flag is what will carve the first one away.

diagnostics.message: Call to `fetchFlaky` escapes this `@nothrow` function: it is declared without a body — an ambient declaration, a `.d.ts`, or a value known only by its function type — and no mark, manifest, overlay or override colors it, so it is assumed to throw. Your outs, in precedence order: bridge this call with `try`/`catch`; assert the color in `nothrow.overrides.json`; install or write an `@nothrow/*` overlay; or, if you own the package, ship a manifest with `nothrow emit`.

`fetchFlaky()` is discarded, so nothing handles a rejection and Node escalates one to an uncaught exception: what produces it is declared without a body — an ambient declaration, a `.d.ts`, or a value known only by its function type — and no mark, manifest, overlay or override colors it, so it is assumed to reject. Your outs, in precedence order: `await` it inside a `try`/`catch`; end the chain with a `.catch(h)` whose handler is non-throwing; assert the color in `nothrow.overrides.json`; install or write an `@nothrow/*` overlay; or, if you own the package, ship a manifest with `nothrow emit`.

This `@nothrow` function returns a promise, so the mark covers its rejection too: nothing in the syntax names the call that produced it, and a parameter, a property, a non-call initializer or a stored partial chain is unknowable from here. Your outs, in precedence order: `await` it inside a `try`/`catch` and return a value instead; assert the producer's color in `nothrow.overrides.json`; install or write an `@nothrow/*` overlay; or, if you own the package, ship a manifest with `nothrow emit`.
